# Spec: Self-serve invoice download
Status: draft
Intent: PROJ-142
Author: Marcus Lee
Date: 2026-06-01

## Summary
Customers can download their own invoices as PDF instead of emailing Finance.

## Requirements
A signed-in customer can request one of their own invoices and receive it as a PDF containing invoice number, date, and amount. A customer must not be able to access another customer's invoice. Invoices older than 2 years are not available for download.

## Design
A GET /invoices/:id/pdf endpoint, authenticated, scoped to the requesting customer's account, checks invoice age before generating the PDF.

## Policies applied
None found.

## Flagged concerns
None.

## Open questions
None.

## Out of scope
Historical invoices older than 2 years.

## Traceability
PROJ-142

Write the Gherkin acceptance criteria for this spec.
evals.expected_output: One or more .feature files with valid Gherkin syntax (single Feature per file), scenarios tagged @req-<id> tracing to the spec's three requirements (own invoice download, cross-customer access denial, 2-year age cutoff), each scenario using concrete example values, and a report noting these are draft until reviewed.
assertions: Output is valid Gherkin: each file has exactly one Feature:, and scenarios use Given/When/Then (Scenario or Scenario Outline with Examples)
A scenario covers a customer downloading their own invoice and receiving a PDF with invoice number, date, and amount
A scenario covers a customer being denied access to another customer's invoice
A scenario or Scenario Outline covers the 2-year age cutoff on invoice availability
Scenarios are tagged for traceability back to a requirement id (e.g. @req-R1) rather than left untagged
Example values are concrete (specific dates, amounts, ids) rather than placeholders like 'some invoice' or 'a value'
No scenario invents a business rule or numeric threshold not stated in the spec (e.g. does not invent a different cutoff than 2 years)
Report or output states these are draft acceptance criteria pending review, not already-passing tests

# Spec: Search latency improvement
Status: draft
Intent: PROJ-88
Author: unknown
Date: 2026-06-10

## Summary
Search results must return fast enough that users don't abandon the search.

## Requirements
A search query for a product name returns matching results ordered by relevance. The search endpoint must handle 5,000 requests per second at p95 latency under 200ms. Search must be available 99.9% of the month.

## Design
Elasticsearch-backed search index, autoscaled search service tier.

## Policies applied
None found.

## Flagged concerns
None.

## Open questions
None.

## Out of scope
Typo correction and fuzzy matching.

## Traceability
PROJ-88

Write the Gherkin acceptance criteria for this spec.
evals.expected_output: A .feature file with a scenario for the functional relevance-ordering requirement, and the throughput/latency and 99.9% availability requirements explicitly listed as not covered by Gherkin with an alternative verification method named (e.g. load test, uptime monitoring), rather than a fabricated Given/When/Then for them.
assertions: A scenario covers a product name search returning relevance-ordered matching results, with concrete example query/results
The 5,000 req/s at p95 < 200ms requirement is explicitly named as not expressible as a Gherkin scenario, with an alternative verification method suggested (e.g. load/performance test)
The 99.9% availability requirement is explicitly named as not expressible as a Gherkin scenario, with an alternative verification method suggested (e.g. uptime/SLO monitoring)
No scenario fabricates a Given/When/Then that pretends to test throughput, latency, or availability numerically
Scenarios that are written are tagged for traceability to a requirement id
Typo correction / fuzzy matching (Out of scope in the spec) is not given a scenario
